title: Nested Return in a Composite Diamond Clock: A Welded-Seam Audit of Phase Projection, Thermal Nulling, and Residual-Burden Migration
lens: independent secondary structural analysis of an external metrology experiment
object_of_study: Nested physical closure in a composite NV-center clock through phase projection, thermal-mode nulling, and post-closure systematic reordering.
main_question: What structural operation occurs when phase-generated contamination is projected away, thermal drift is nulled, the target oscillator mode is preserved, and a previously subdominant residual becomes governing?

claim_layers.claim: Lourette et al. (SRC-000048) report a composite diamond-clock scheme in which TTZFS-8 eight-phase cycling suppresses pulse-error-generated spectral components and a composite D/Q estimator nulls first-order thermal drift while preserving the common oscillator mode (as read by the local analysis).

The local analysis (SRC-000049) reads the two operations as a typed, hierarchical local closure: phase-space projection followed by channel-space thermal nulling; once the dominant thermal burden is suppressed a new leading residual becomes visible.
These local operators are Tier-2 labels for native physical operations; they do not redefine canonical tau_R or the reserved invariants.

No Tier-0 UMCP weld verdict is claimed: the source lacks a GCD return contract, seam-accounting profile, return-credit definition, residual tolerance, and RunID; 'welded-seam audit' names the audit burden, not a pre-granted weld.
